category_title: Adolescents with ADHD exhibiting low levels of agency, chronic procrastination, and disorganized academic behaviors
minimal_context: The student is sitting at a separate desk in a quiet environment attempting to memorize facts for an upcoming test.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Please sit at this separate desk away from the window and start memorizing these facts for your upcoming test.

STUDENT: I don’t find myself a very effective studier … ’cause I can’t concentrate.

TUTOR: Just try to focus on the material. What is going through your mind right now while you look at the study materials?

STUDENT: Man this is boring! Mostly just music, or nothing really.

TUTOR: You need to keep trying to memorize the facts so you can pass the exam.

STUDENT: Studying’s just stupid ’cause it doesn’t work. I can never master these basic skills, I guess I'm just too lazy to do things that take this much mental effort.

options.A: Using mnemonic strategies (keyword, pegword, and letter mnemonics) to help the student memorize the facts.
options.B: Withholding attention when the student engages in problem behavior during the study session.
options.C: Incorporating active, hands-on tasks and opportunities for peer discussion and interaction into the study session.
options.D: Ignoring all undesirable behaviors exhibited by the student while they are attempting to memorize facts.
